title: First union in New Orleans and sitting in around the district
summary: Humphrey recalls the arrival of the union, casual sitting-in before it, and sending trombonist George Washington to Ma Rainey's cast.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: It wasn't like it is now. Of course, they... We was working there when they formed the first union.

But now... When that, uh... Before they put the union in here... And... Fellas come around, you don't want to sit in, you know, something like that. Okay, man. Blow something for me. Well, I'd go back to town, you know, man. Color cap there is. How long you don't stay? That's all right. I'd be here to come back. Well, I'd go back there. Where George and Boyd in there, most playing. Honest... Uh... Playin' back in the district back there. Hang out around there, George Washington. And... Well, that drum won't come there and relieve me, you know.

Well, I'd come back and... Just by the time I knew they were gonna close up, see. Well, I know the man ain't made no money. You know, I'm working regular. Yeah, man. Paying this much I made for the whole side. You know, the nice side. Mm-hmm. Well, that's how we used to get along. I had a little fella named George Washington. Nice trombone player. I sent him in here for a moment. Laughhead, do's at him. Him and his wife. He was out there with more rain in. They wasn't doing nothing. Wasn't makin' no money. I said, man. I was playing with Eve Ann Thomas. Black Eagle Band. I said, man, you wanna go in home?

I said, man. I said, man. I said, man. I can't get any out of this fella's thick. I said, man. I can't get any out of this fella's thick. I said, you ain't doing nothing out of here, man. You're sleeping in the station here waiting for Ma Rainey to... get some tickets from Baton Rouge or somewhere to pull you all in there. And then two chairs in one. She's gonna take all the money. She's gonna take all the money. Still ain't gonna have nothing.
